name: Chat PR worktree
description:
## 5-Line Summary

1. **Goal:** let a chat bind to a git worktree so agents read/save files there, with child tasks (any nesting depth) inheriting it, enabling parallel branches and test environments.
2. **Finding:** the only file root used everywhere is `settings.abs_project_path`; git worktree plumbing already exists (`git_worktrees_path`, `_create_branch_worktree`, `create_pr_branch(worktree=True)`), but the file/engine/tool layers are worktree-blind.
3. **Impact:** ~45 files listed and prioritized (P0/P1/P2) across data model, engines, tools, API, SIO, knowledge/watchers, plus 3 new modules; key traps are path allow-lists rejecting worktrees outside the repo, `is_git_root` on a `.git` file, missing `.codx` in worktrees, and shared cached settings objects.
4. **Recommendation:** phase 0 attach existing PR worktree to the chat → phase 1 `Chat.worktree` + resolver + `settings.for_root()` (approach A) → phase 2 API scoping + CRUD → phase 3 knowledge/wiki policy, watcher exclusions, retention, docker integration; long-term target is a chat-scoped session (approach C).
5. **Blocked on decisions:** inheritance style, default opt-in vs automatic, knowledge/RAG policy, worktree creation trigger, cleanup policy, and non-git project handling.

Chat worktree (git worktree). We'll be able to associate a worktree with a chat. That will affect to the tools reading and saving files. Children tasks (no matter nested level) will inherit.

The goal is to have multiple branches and test environments running in parallel for the agents. 

Analyze whole api and find potential issues, generate full list of files affected with a description of the change (no coding yet).

After your analysis, suggest a better approach or alternatives for this, if any.

I'll analyze the codebase to understand how files are read/saved and how tasks/chats are structured, then identify where worktree support would impact things.# Chat worktree — architecture analysis ## 1. Objective (restated) - A **chat** (and therefore every agent run started from it) must be able to operate on a **git worktree** instead of the project's main checkout. - All **file-reading and file-saving** code paths must resolve paths against that worktree. - **Child tasks inherit** the worktree, at any nesting depth. - Enables **parallel branches / parallel test environments** for concurrent agents. - Deliverable now: impact analysis + full file list with the change description + alternatives. **No code yet.** --- ## 2. How file access works today (the constraint) There is exactly **one** root used everywhere: `CODXJuniorSettings.abs_project_path`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[HTTP /api/*] --> M[app.py middleware
CODXJuniorSession
from x-codx-path] B[SIO event] --> S1[sio_api_endpoint
CODXJuniorSession] M --> S1 S1 --> T[SmolAgent._execute_tool
params settings = session.settings] T --> TL[tools/*
settings.abs_project_path] S1 --> FE[FileEngine
settings.abs_project_path] S1 --> CE[CodeEngine / GitEngine
settings.abs_project_path] ``` Key facts gathered: | Fact | Where | |---|---| | Session is built **per request** from `codx_path`; no chat context at that point | `app.py` → `get_codx_junior_session`, `sio/sio.py:sio_api_endpoint` | | Tools receive the **shared project settings object** (`tool_settings["project_settings"]` → `params["settings"] = self.settings`) | `ai/smol/smol_agent.py:_execute_tool` | | Chat context is already propagated to tools through `settings._active_session` + `session._current_chat` | `smol_agent.py:_run_chat_loop`, used by `tools/git_tools.py` and `create_task`/`process_task` | | Worktree support **already exists** for PR branches (`git_worktrees_path`, `get_worktrees_path()`, `_create_branch_worktree`, `list_worktrees`, `_remove_worktree`, `create_pr_branch(use_worktree=True)`, `pr_view.worktree_path`) | `settings.py`, `engine/git_engine.py`, `tools/git_tools.py` | | Nothing in the **file layer** knows about worktrees | `engine/file_engine.py`, `tools/project_tools.py`, `engine/code_engine.py` | | Sub-task creation already copies `project_id`, `board`, `column` — but there is no worktree field to copy | `engine/chat_engine_actions.py`, `tools/create_task_tool.py` | So ~90% of the git plumbing exists; what's missing is **a workspace scope** in the read/write layer plus **inheritance on the chat tree**. --- ## 3. Proposed model (to be implemented later) ``` Chat └── worktree: ChatWorktree | None branch, path, base_branch, status, created_at, created_by ``` Resolution rule (single function, used by every layer): ``` resolve_chat_workspace(chat) -> root_path 1. chat.worktree.path (if valid + registered) 2. else walk parent_id chain (nested, cycle-guarded, max depth) 3. else settings.abs_project_path (current behaviour) ``` Effective root feeds **three distinct concepts** that today are all `abs_project_path`: | Concept | Meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | `workspace_root` | where files are read/written | `/…/app-worktrees/chat-abc` | | `repo_root` | the git repository (common `.git`) | `/…/app` | | `codx_path` | project metadata (chats, knowledge, wiki) | `/…/app/.codx` | **Only `workspace_root` moves.** `codx_path` must stay on the project so chats/kanban/knowledge remain shared — otherwise the chat that owns the worktree can't even find its own task files. --- ## 4. Full list of affected files Legend: **P0** = breaks/needed for the feature to work at all · **P1** = correctness/leaks · **P2** = polish. ### 4.1 Data model & persistence | File | Prio | Change | |---|---|---| | `codx/junior/db.py` | P0 | Add `ChatWorktree` model and `Chat.worktree: Optional[ChatWorktree]`. Pydantic `model_dump()` already persists it → no storage migration for existing chats (defaults to `None` = current behaviour). Consider `Message.worktree_path` only if per-message scope is wanted (a message already has `project_id`; adding a second scope axis must be documented to avoid a 2×2 precedence matrix). | | `codx/junior/chat_manager.py` | P0 | On `save_chat`: validate/normalise `worktree.path`; when a chat has `parent_id` and no worktree, **copy the parent's** (explicit inheritance, so a re-parented/orphaned task keeps its branch). Cross-cutting issues to resolve before coding 1. **Path allow-list vs. worktree location.** `_create_branch_worktree` *requires* the worktree to be **outside** the repository. Meanwhile `file_engine._resolve_absolute_path`, `project_tools` (`startswith(settings.abs_project_path)`), `apply_file_changes._secure_path_check` and `code_engine` all **reject** paths outside the project. ⇒ Every read/write tool must be taught the workspace root, or nothing works. This is the #1 trap. 2. **`is_git_root` is wrong in worktrees** (`os.path.isdir(.git)`; a worktree has a `.git` *file*). 3. **`.codx` does not exist in a worktree** (untracked/ignored) → no `project.json`, no chats, no knowledge. Sessions must keep `codx_path` on the main project and only swap the *file root*. 4. **Don't mutate shared settings.** `find_all_projects()` caches `CODXJuniorSettings` objects process-wide; setting `abs_project_path` per chat would leak between concurrent agents. Use a derived copy or an explicit root. 5. **Branch checkout collision.** `create_pr_branch(use_worktree=False)` does `git checkout` in the main tree; a branch already checked out in a worktree cannot be checked out again → error paths and a UX decision (default should be worktree mode once this exists). 6. **Git index locks.** N chats × N worktrees running `git add`/`commit` concurrently (`write_file` auto-stages!) will produce `index.lock` contention and surprise staging on the main tree. 7. **Knowledge / RAG divergence.** The index is built on the main tree; worktree files are neither indexed nor discoverable, and knowledge hits return main-tree paths. Options: (a) disable knowledge for worktree chats, (b) namespace a collection per worktree, (c) map main→worktree paths on read. 8. **Wiki pollution.** `WikiEngine` writes into the shared `codx_path/wiki`. 9. **Watchers/indexers** (`background.py`, `ChangeManager`) may re-index worktree copies or trigger `@mentions` rewrites inside branches. 10. **Security.** `chat.worktree.path` arrives from client JSON in `PUT /api/chats`. It must be validated against the configured worktrees base **and** the live `git worktree list`; otherwise it's an arbitrary-filesystem read/write primitive given the tool allow-lists above. 11. **Ambiguity of relative paths.** Today `FileEngine` falls back across the project **and child projects**; with a second root, precedence must be defined (`workspace → child projects → error`). 12. **Scope matrix.** `Message.project_id` (turn project) × `Chat.worktree` (workspace) × `Chat.owner_project_id` (persistence) = 3 axes; write the precedence rules explicitly or agents will write to the wrong tree. 13. **Disk / lifecycle.** Worktrees are full working copies; need retention policy, prune on abandon/close, cleanup on `delete_project`, and a cap per project. --- ## 6. Alternatives & recommendation | # | Approach | Pros | Cons | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---| | **A** | **Derived settings per workspace** — `settings.for_root(worktree)` returns a copy with `abs_project_path` overridden; injected into tools. Almost all existing `settings.abs_project_path` code keeps working. | Smallest diff, fast to ship, backwards compatible (`worktree=None` → identical object) | Hidden coupling; must guarantee the copy is not cached/mutated; `is_git_root`/`codx_path` need care; easy to bypass accidentally | **Recommended as phase 1** | | **B** | **Explicit threading** — `root_path`/`workspace` parameter passed through `FileEngine` + every tool signature | Explicit, testable, no hidden state | Touches ~30 signatures; tools are LLM-facing (`**kwargs`) so risk of forgetting one is high | Phase 2 hardening | | **C** | **Chat-scoped session** — one `CODXJuniorSession` per (project, workspace) exposing `abs_workspace_path`;
